theater: 伊比利亞半島葡萄牙與西班牙邊境

battle.name: 橘子戰爭
battle.theater: 伊比利亞半島葡萄牙與西班牙邊境
battle.brief: 一八〇一年二月十九日，西班牙以奧利文薩的邊界爭端為由向葡萄牙宣戰，交火落在伊比利亞半島邊境的阿連特茹與阿爾加維。葡軍退守洛萊與埃爾瓦斯一帶堡壘，西軍在阿爾布費拉得手，雙方五月簽訂和約。英軍分遣隊攜帶的一七五七年式步槍，是英國線列步兵的制式火槍，亦隨軍械供應裝備葡軍。

kit.name: 一七五七年式步槍
kit.history: 一七五七年式步槍是英國陸軍線列步兵的制式火槍，配置於步兵連與營的射擊單位，屬於步兵部隊的基本地面槍械。

countries: 一八〇一年的橘子戰爭，名義上的交戰方只有葡萄牙王國與西班牙王國，但兩國背後各站著歐洲的兩股力量。葡萄牙由女王瑪麗亞一世與攝政王若昂主持國政，軍隊骨幹是十餘個線列步兵營與若干炮兵連，另有地方民兵與義勇分隊待命；作戰重點在阿爾加維與阿連特茹一帶的邊境，前線據點由洛萊、埃爾瓦斯、胡羅梅尼亞以及瓜迪阿納河兩岸的舊日工事串聯，防守縱深一直伸到里斯本外圍。西班牙由卡洛斯四世統治，內閣與戰爭的實際推手是首相戈多伊，他主張以軍事手段迫令里斯本關閉港口、限制英國商船入港；入侵縱隊由步兵營、輕型野戰炮、工兵與輜重分隊組成，沿瓜迪阿納河東岸與邊境道路推進，兵鋒直指里斯本方向。英國不是條約交戰國，但自一七九三年起便與葡萄牙訂有同盟，戰事一開便派皇家海軍分遣隊巡弋葡西近海，另以約七百五十人的分遣隊在奧埃拉斯登陸，軍火、年金與海運補給也源源送抵葡軍。幕後的推力來自法國：法國與西班牙在一八〇〇年訂立條約後，英國擔心法國取得葡國港口，要求里斯本切斷對法貿易，葡萄牙正因夾在中間而不得不向倫敦求援。這是一場在歐洲海上對抗的背景下爆發的邊界戰爭，前線在數百公里邊境上拉開，真正決定勝負的卻是里斯本的防衛與近海的封鎖。
countriesEn: The War of the Oranges of 1801 had only two nominal belligerents, the Kingdom of Portugal and the Kingdom of Spain, yet behind each of them stood a different power of Europe. Portugal was governed by Queen Maria I and the Prince Regent John, with a military whose backbone was a dozen or more line infantry battalions and a number of artillery companies, supplemented by provincial militia and volunteer detachments. Its fighting weight lay along the border of the Algarve and the Alentejo, where a chain of positions, Loulé, Elvas, Juromenha and the older works on both banks of the Guadiana, led back to a defensive depth that reached the outskirts of Lisbon. Spain was ruled by Charles IV, while the effective driver of the war was the prime minister Godoy, who wanted military means to force Lisbon to close its ports and bar British shipping. His invading column was built from infantry battalions, light field guns, engineers and trains, and it advanced along the east bank of the Guadiana and the border roads with Lisbon in view. Britain was not a party to the treaties, but it had been in alliance with Portugal since 1793: as soon as hostilities began it sent a Royal Navy detachment into the waters off Portugal and landed a force of about 750 men at Oeiras, while money, munitions and sea transport flowed to the Portuguese army. The hidden pressure came from France. After the treaty of 1800 between France and Spain, Britain feared that France would take Portuguese ports and demanded that Lisbon cut her trade with France, and Portugal, caught between them, had no choice but to turn to London. This was a border war fought in the shadow of a wider European struggle at sea, with the front extended along hundreds of kilometres of frontier, though what really decided the outcome was the defence of Lisbon and the blockade lying off the coast.
people: 里斯本方面，攝政王若昂（後來的若昂六世）是真正的決策者；女王瑪麗亞一世此時健康惡化，幾乎不問政事，戰事一開便急向倫敦求援。葡軍的靈魂是英國少將威廉·卡爾·貝雷斯福德，他以英軍將領的身分替葡軍整編編制、訓練射擊與供應線，被葡廷倚為最高軍事顧問兼實際指揮者；前線的步兵戰鬥多由荷蘭入籍葡萄牙的將領亨里克·德·施米爾姆彭寧率領，阿爾布費拉一役的野戰指揮即出於他。英國方面，率軍在奧埃拉斯登陸並擔任葡方軍事聯絡的是理查德·比克頓中將，他帶來的分遣隊雖未投入阿爾布費拉會戰，卻是葡廷與倫敦之間的樞紐；倫敦方面，首相小威廉·皮特與陸軍大臣亨利·鄧達斯把援助葡萄牙視為阻止法國取得伊比利亞半島港口的一環，撥付的軍費遠超一場邊界衝突所需。西班牙的指揮體系，決策集中在馬德里的軍政當局，首相戈多伊幾乎親自過問每一步驟；前線則由數名旅級將領輪流指揮，其中利奧波多·奧唐奈當時已是旅長，參與了阿爾加維方面的作戰，日後更以半島戰爭與西班牙自由派的領袖身分聞名。關於雙方傷亡人數，各家記載互相矛盾、無從核對，本實錄因此不列任何看似精確的傷亡數字。
peopleEn: In Lisbon the real decision maker was the Prince Regent John, later John VI of Portugal; Queen Maria I was in poor health at the time and took almost no part in government, and the moment war broke out the court appealed to London for help. The soul of the Portuguese army was the British major general William Carr Beresford, who served as a British officer in the reform of the Portuguese establishment, of its drill and of its supply system, and was trusted by the court as chief military adviser and effective commander in the field. The infantry fighting in the border was led for the most part by Henrique de Schimmelpennig, a Dutchman by birth in Portuguese service, and it was he who held the field command at the battle of Albufeira. On the British side the officer who landed at Oeiras and served as the link with the Portuguese command was Major General Richard Bickerton; although his detachment was never committed to the fighting at Albufeira, it was the hinge between the court at Lisbon and the government at home. In London, the prime minister the younger William Pitt and the secretary of state for war Henry Dundas treated the support of Portugal as a means of denying French access to Iberian ports, and the money they voted was out of all proportion to a border clash. On the Spanish side the direction of the war was concentrated in the military authorities in Madrid, and the prime minister Godoy followed almost every step himself; in the field the command passed between several brigade generals, among them Leopoldo O'Donnell, already a brigade leader then, who took part in the operations in the Algarve and was later known as a leader of the Spanish liberals and of the Peninsular War. Casualty figures for the two sides are mutually contradictory and cannot be checked against one another, so no figure that looks precise is given here.
kits: 本卡兵器一七五七年式步槍，是英國陸軍自一七五七年起列裝的制式滑膛燧發步槍，也是十八世紀末至十九世紀初英軍線列步兵的基本地面槍械。槍身為長約四十二吋的一點零六公尺單身管，口徑約零點五七英吋，配燧發機件，燧石由可翻起的護板壓住而點燃底火；槍口原留插銷式刺刀的位置，後改裝矛式刺刀，一七八二年式的矛式刺刀是當時英軍的標準配備。發射用火藥、鉛彈與火帽分裝，每兵標準備彈六十發，射速約每分鐘三至四發，有效射程約二百公尺，超出此距彈道便急遽失準。在橘子戰爭中，這件兵器由英國分遣隊攜帶，並以英國軍械庫的存量逐步補充葡萄牙線列步兵；葡軍各營裝備並不一致，部分營仍沿用十八世紀中葉的舊式火槍。西班牙線列步兵使用西班牙自製的十八世紀燧發滑膛步槍，口徑約零點五八英吋，同樣以刺刀作近戰兵器，並未普遍改用雷管槍。炮兵方面，英葡分隊配六磅滑膛野戰炮，西班牙縱隊另有八磅與十二磅炮，圍攻奧利文薩時還調用更重的攻城炮；邊境要塞如胡羅梅尼亞與埃爾瓦斯一帶的堡壘則架設青銅炮與舊式鐵炮。運輸依靠牛車與騾隊，彈藥分載於營部彈藥箱、炮架箱與彈藥車，各營每日耗彈量無從核實。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card, the Pattern 1757 Musket, was the standard smoothbore flintlock musket adopted by the British army from 1757 and the basic infantry arm of the line battalions from the late eighteenth into the early nineteenth century. It had a single barrel about forty-two inches long, that is roughly 1.06 metres, of about 0.577 inch calibre, worked by a flintlock in which the flint was held by a pivoted frizzen that struck the pan; the muzzle had originally been drilled to take a plug bayonet and was later fitted for the socket bayonet, the socket bayonet of 1782 being the standard of the British army at the time. It fired loose ammunition of powder, ball and priming, with sixty rounds per man as the standard issue, a rate of fire of about three to four rounds a minute and an effective range of some two hundred metres, beyond which the fall of shot was rapidly lost. In the War of the Oranges this arm was carried by the British detachment and was passed on to the Portuguese line infantry from the stores of the British ordnance; the equipment of the Portuguese battalions was not uniform, and some still used older eighteenth century muskets. The Spanish line infantry used Spanish-made eighteenth century flintlock muskets of about 0.58 inch calibre, likewise with the bayonet for close work, and had not yet gone over to percussion generally. In the artillery arm, the British and Portuguese detachments had six-pounder smoothbore field guns, the Spanish column had eight and twelve pounders as well, and heavier siege guns were brought up against Olivença; the frontier works at Juromenha and around Elvas mounted bronze and older iron guns. Transport was by ox cart and mule, ammunition was carried in regimental ammunition boxes, on limber boxes and in ammunition wagons, and no daily rate of consumption can be verified for any battalion.
tactics: 西班牙入侵縱隊渡過瓜迪阿納河之後，沒有沿整條葡境展開漫長的正面消耗，而是集中兵力於通向里斯本的主要道路，企圖速戰速決；其進展以步兵縱隊為主，前有輕型野戰炮開路，遇葡軍堅固據點便改為封鎖包圍，先以炮火壓制射界，再以步兵佔領可以控制道路的高地。胡羅梅尼亞與奧利文薩兩處要塞在戰爭首月互相對峙、彼此炮擊，葡軍利用棱堡射界拖住西班牙縱隊，迫使對方分兵。葡軍整體採取守勢與遲滯抵抗，盡量避免在開闊河岸與西班牙縱隊決戰，依次退守能控制道路的高地與既有堡壘，並把民兵與地方武裝編入沿線據點，構成多層次的抵抗。貝雷斯福德整編之後，葡軍把英軍分遣隊與最精銳的骨幹營留在里斯本附近作為預備隊，寧可讓邊線受壓也不投入正面會戰。阿爾布費拉一役，葡軍把步兵分布在城區及鄰近高地，野戰炮與步兵互相支援，構成可以互相掩護的正面；西班牙軍先以炮兵射擊固定葡軍各點，再讓多個步兵縱隊分別接近中央與兩翼，葡軍正面在持續炮火下被逐段瓦解，缺口出現後各部相互捲入，陣線因而崩潰，葡軍沿內陸道路北撤。西軍雖然得手，卻沒有把戰果轉化為對里斯本的追擊，一半因自身損失與補給線拉長，一半因英軍分遣隊與皇家海軍分遣隊就泊在里斯本外海。現有史料足以確認上述戰術階段，卻不足以為每個步兵營指定射擊路線與個別射界。
tacticsEn: After crossing the Guadiana, the Spanish invading column did not grind along the whole Portuguese frontier in a long war of attrition; it concentrated on the main roads that led to Lisbon in the hope of a quick decision. Its advance was made in infantry columns with light field guns in front, and when it met a strong Portuguese position it changed to blockade and envelopment, first silencing the field of fire with artillery and then occupying heights that commanded the road. The works at Juromenha and Olivença faced each other and exchanged fire through the first weeks of the war, and the Portuguese used the angled fire of their bastions to hold the Spanish column in place and force it to divide. On the Portuguese side the plan as a whole was one of defence and delaying action: open river banks were avoided rather than challenged by a decisive battle, the army fell back in turn on the heights and the old works that commanded the roads, and the militia and local armed bands were woven into the line of posts to make a defence in several layers. After Beresford's reform the British detachment and the best of the line battalions were kept near Lisbon as a reserve, and the border was allowed to be pressed rather than risking a general action. At Albufeira the Portuguese posted their infantry in the town and on the neighbouring heights, with the field guns in mutual support so that infantry and guns covered one another. The Spanish opened with artillery fire that pinned each Portuguese point in turn, then brought several infantry columns against the centre and the flanks together; the Portuguese front was broken up piece by piece under the sustained fire, the gaps drew the separate units into one another, and the line collapsed, the retreat being made northward along the inland roads. Even so the Spaniards did not convert the victory into a pursuit of Lisbon, in part because of their own losses and the lengthening of their supply line and in part because the British detachment and the Royal Navy squadron lay just off the Portuguese capital. The surviving material is enough to confirm those stages of the fighting, but not enough to assign a firing line or a specific field of fire to each infantry battalion.
data: 可寫而有根據的數字有限，且各家的記載互相矛盾。時間線較為確定：邊界衝突起於一八〇一年一月十八日前後，一批西班牙士兵越過邊界進入奧利文薩一帶，葡軍要求其退出，隨後引發互擾與擲橘的插曲；西班牙於二月十九日宣布開戰，葡萄牙於二月二十日宣戰，戰爭自此起算。三月二十四日，坎普馬約爾一線爆發戰鬥；三月二十七日，理查德·比克頓率領的英軍分遣隊在奧埃拉斯登陸，皇家海軍分遣隊同時進入葡西近海；三月二十八日，阿爾布費拉會戰開打，西班牙以約六千人的縱隊進攻，葡軍據守者約四千至五千人。兵力估計因是否計入民兵與輔助部隊而異，英軍分遣隊一般記為約七百五十人。距離上，里斯本至埃爾瓦斯約二百二十公里，埃爾瓦斯至奧利文薩約二十公里，阿爾布費拉距里斯本約一百四十公里，瓜迪阿納河是縱隊越境的主要門戶。五月二十五日，奧利文薩要塞守軍投降，比條約生效早五日；五月三十日，葡西在巴達霍斯簽訂和約，自開戰至此歷時約三個月又十一天。傷亡方面沒有可信的統一統計，可確定的只是阿爾布費拉一役葡軍有數百人陣亡、受傷與被俘，西軍亦付出數百人的代價，具體數目各方說法互相矛盾，本實錄不予填補。就火力節奏而言，一七五七年式步槍每兵備彈六十發、射速每分鐘三至四發，是當時線列步兵的射擊基準。
dataEn: The numbers that can be written down with some foundation are few, and the accounts of them contradict one another. The sequence of events is the firmest part. The border clash began around the eighteenth of January 1801, when a body of Spanish soldiers crossed the frontier into the district of Olivença; the Portuguese demanded their withdrawal, and quarrels and the business of the thrown oranges followed. Spain declared war on the nineteenth of February and Portugal answered on the twentieth, and the war is counted from there. Fighting broke out along the line of Campo Maior on the twenty-fourth of March; on the twenty-seventh the British detachment under Richard Bickerton landed at Oeiras while a Royal Navy squadron entered the waters between Portugal and Spain; on the twenty-eighth the battle of Albufeira was fought, the Spanish attacking with a column of about six thousand men against four to five thousand Portuguese in the defences. The strength estimates differ according to whether militia and auxiliary troops are counted, and the British detachment is generally given as about seven hundred and fifty men. As to distances, Lisbon is about two hundred and twenty kilometres from Elvas by road, Elvas is about twenty kilometres from Olivença, Albufeira lies about a hundred and forty kilometres from Lisbon, and the Guadiana was the gateway by which the column crossed into Portugal. On the twenty-fifth of May the garrison of the fortress of Olivença surrendered, five days before the treaty took effect; on the thirtieth of May Portugal and Spain signed the peace at Badajoz, about three months and eleven days after the war began. There is no reliable overall casualty return: what can be said is that at Albufeira the Portuguese had several hundred men killed, wounded and taken prisoner, and that the Spaniards paid a similar cost, the exact figures being mutually contradictory, so none is supplied here. As for the rhythm of fire, the Pattern 1757 musket with sixty rounds per man and a rate of three to four shots a minute sets the firing standard of the line infantry of the time.
cause: 橘子戰爭的起因是三件事疊在一起。第一件是邊界本身就不清楚：一七五〇年《馬德里條約》重新劃定葡西邊界時，奧利文薩及其周邊村落的歸屬在條約文字、實際控制與居民認同之間長期不一致，一八〇〇年前後西班牙軍方曾數次進入葡方視為己有的據點，爭議遂從法律問題變成軍事佔領問題。第二件是西班牙的封鎖要求：法國在一八〇〇年與西班牙訂立條約後，英國擔心法國取得葡國港口，要求里斯本切斷對法貿易；戈多伊以此為由，向葡萄牙提出最後通牒，要求關閉港口、驅逐英國商船，里斯本拖延不答。第三件是同盟的作用：葡萄牙自一七九三年起倚英國為屏障，一旦西班牙開戰，葡廷立刻向倫敦求援，英國的海上封鎖與陸軍分遣隊因此直接介入。至於「橘子」這個名稱，通行說法是葡國士兵在邊界衝突中把從俘虜那裡取來的橘子擲回西班牙士兵；細節版本各異，有的說葡軍主動擲橘趕人，有的說西軍在撤退途中被擲。它解釋了稱號的來歷，卻不是開戰的真正理由，邊界、封鎖與同盟才是。
causeEn: Three things came together to bring about the War of the Oranges. The first was that the frontier itself was not clearly drawn. When the Treaty of Madrid of 1750 set the Portuguese and Spanish border afresh, the ownership of Olivença and of the villages around it remained inconsistent between the words of the treaty, actual control on the ground and the identity claimed by the inhabitants, and around 1800 Spanish troops more than once entered places that the Portuguese regarded as their own, so that the dispute turned from a matter of law into a matter of military occupation. The second was the Spanish demand for a blockade: after the treaty of 1800 between France and Spain, Britain grew afraid that France would take Portuguese ports and pressed Lisbon to cut her trade with France; Godoy used this as his pretext and put a last warning to Portugal, requiring her ports to be closed and British shipping driven out, and Lisbon delayed her answer. The third was the alliance: Portugal had leaned on Britain as her shield since 1793, and the moment Spain went to war the court at Lisbon appealed to London, which brought the British naval blockade and a British detachment on shore directly into the war. As for the name, the account usually given is that Portuguese soldiers took oranges from the saddlebags of prisoners and threw them back at Spanish soldiers during a border clash; the details differ, some telling that the Portuguese threw the oranges to drive the Spaniards away and others that the Spaniards were pelted as they withdrew. The story explains the title, but it is not the real reason for the war; the frontier, the blockade and the alliance are.
impact: 對葡萄牙而言，這場戰爭的直接結果是保住國土，間接結果是把國家更深地綁在英國身上。葡軍在阿爾布費拉受挫，卻沒有崩潰；貝雷斯福德整編的線列步兵、炮兵與後勤體系自此成為英國在半島上倚重的支撐，葡國的港口與兵源開始定期供應英軍，而英國的撥款、軍官與軍械也持續流入葡軍，這種互賴在後來的半島戰爭中成為英國陸軍在伊比利亞立足的基礎。對西班牙而言，這是一場得不償失的勝利：阿爾布費拉的戰術成功沒有帶來里斯本，戈多伊的封鎖要求完全落空，戰爭卻留下一個「橘子」的笑柄，馬德里的宮廷與輿論都飽受嘲弄。更長遠的影響落在邊界上，奧利文薩的歸屬並未因條約而真正解決：一八一一年葡萄牙軍隊曾重新佔領該地，一八一五年維也納會議確認其歸屬西班牙，葡萄牙從此把收回奧利文薩當作國家目標，直到一八六一年的戰爭中再度拿下並保留至今。從大格局看，這場戰爭是拿破崙時代英國在伊比利亞半島爭奪港口與資源的一環，它把葡萄牙推上反法同盟的前線，也加深了葡西兩國的世仇。
impactEn: For Portugal the direct result of the war was the preservation of the country, and the indirect result was a tighter binding of the nation to Britain. The Portuguese army was checked at Albufeira but did not break: the line infantry, artillery and supply system reformed by Beresford became a support on which Britain relied in the peninsula, Portuguese ports and manpower began to feed the British army on a regular basis, and British money, officers and stores continued to flow into the Portuguese army, and that reciprocity in the later Peninsular War became the foundation on which the British army stood in Iberia. For Spain it was a victory that cost more than it gained: the tactical success at Albufeira brought no Lisbon, Godoy's demands for a blockade came to nothing, and the war left behind the laughing stock of the oranges, mocked in the Madrid court and in public opinion. The longer effect fell on the frontier, for the ownership of Olivença was not really settled by the treaty: Portuguese troops occupied the town again in 1811, the Congress of Vienna confirmed it to Spain in 1815, and Portugal from then on treated the recovery of Olivença as a national aim, until in the war of 1861 it was taken a third time and kept. Seen in the wider frame, this war was one of the English struggles for Iberian ports and resources in the age of Napoleon; it pushed Portugal to the front of the anti-French coalition and deepened the enmity between the two Iberian kingdoms.
result: 一八〇一年五月三十日，葡萄牙與西班牙在巴達霍斯簽訂和約，結束了正面作戰。按條約，西班牙把奧利文薩及其鄰近地區割予葡萄牙，葡萄牙則退出西班牙軍隊佔領的其他葡境據點，並就條約所列的財政補償作出安排，雙方另派員勘定界線，爭議最烈的奧利文薩一帶劃歸葡萄牙。奧利文薩要塞守軍在五月二十五日便已投降歸葡，比條約生效早五日，和平在戰場上先於文件到來。西班牙的實際收穫是保住軍隊完整，並在阿爾加維一度佔領若干城鎮，但沒有封閉葡國港口、沒有扣留英國商船、也沒有推進到里斯本的城牆之下；葡國則保住阿爾加維與通往里斯本的北部防線，代價是接受奧利文薩的割讓與一筆財政讓步，並承認英國在防衛上的主導角色。英軍分遣隊在西班牙撤軍之後離去，皇家海軍也結束近海施壓。戰後各方的評論眾說紛紜：西班牙把失敗歸咎於前線指揮與補給，葡軍內部則為阿爾布費拉的損失與貝雷斯福德的責任爭論不休，這些指責至今仍留在戰史記載之中。
resultEn: On the thirtieth of May 1801 Portugal and Spain signed the peace at Badajoz, which ended the fighting in earnest. Under its terms Spain ceded Olivença and the neighbouring district to Portugal; Portugal withdrew from the other positions in Portuguese territory held by the Spanish army and made the financial compensation set out in the treaty, while the two sides sent commissioners to mark out the frontier, the most disputed ground, that of Olivença itself, passing to Portugal. The garrison of the fortress of Olivença had already surrendered to the Portuguese on the twenty-fifth of May, five days before the treaty took effect, so that peace reached the battlefield before it reached the paper. Spain's real gains were an intact army and temporary possession of a few towns in the Algarve, but no Portuguese port was closed, no British ship was detained and nothing was carried to the walls of Lisbon. Portugal kept the Algarve and the northern line of defence on the capital, at the price of accepting the cession of Olivença and a financial concession, and of acknowledging the leading part played by Britain in her defence. The British detachment left once the Spaniards had withdrawn, and the Royal Navy ended its pressure on the coast. The comments of the time are divided: Spain blamed the conduct of the front and the supply system, while inside the Portuguese army the losses at Albufeira and the responsibility of Beresford were argued over at length, and those accusations remain in the histories.
